findings.title: A rival as entrusted principal
findings.claim: In the opening pericope, assigning another deity can also touch delegated reliance: after God makes the Book guidance, the warning bars taking anyone besides Him as wakil, so placing an ilah beside Allah can function as appointing an alternate principal for what one entrusts.
findings.mechanism: The focus's status-setting verb and indefinite deity object meet 17:2's entrusted wakil and its prohibition on taking someone apart from God; 17:1 frames the human as servant. The contact changes a rival from only a second named deity into a possible office of ultimate reliance.
findings.reader_payoff: The rival becomes legible as a competing party to whom trust and responsibility might be handed.
findings.containment: The wakil wording may only sharpen the prohibition, without making every delegated role worship. The focus still plainly prohibits adding a deity alongside God.

epistemic.reason: The exact 17:1-2 surfaces and focus coordinates are supplied, but the contextual synthesis comes from a legacy_unbound HFT trace; its entrusted-principal inference remains attributed.

findings.title: Aid turned into immobility

findings.mechanism: The focus's taqʿuda and makhdulan carry withdrawal from action and loss of support; 17:6 supplies aid and a mobilized company, and 17:8 ends the earlier reversal in confinement. Their contact turns forsakenness from mere absence of a helper into a reversal from mobilization to isolation and arrested movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning's outcome becomes bodily and social: support does not arrive, the person is held back, and the active company continues without them.
findings.containment: The collective history may be an analogy for an individual consequence. The focus still says blamed and forsaken; neither a literal imprisonment nor a physical illness is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The 17:6 and 17:8 surfaces, coordinates, and focus carriers agree with the packet; the collective-to-individual reversal and attributed branch roles remain qualified.

findings.mechanism: The focus supplies sitting, held-back action, and a weak-leg branch; 17:9 supplies gentle guidance and uprightness. The contrast changes the consequence from blame alone into a possible loss of moral and practical capacity to stand.
findings.reader_payoff: The earlier promise of a guided, upright course gains a bodily counter-image in the focus's seated and weakened endpoint.
findings.containment: Taqʿuda may simply mark becoming fixed in a state, leaving posture as resonance. The disease-specific qʿd facet does not establish that the person is ill or disabled, and the focus's warning and blame remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The exact 17:9 root and word coordinates return to focus words, but the posture-to-guidance relation is carried by an unbound HFT trace and the disease-specific facet is only bounded as a possibility.

findings.reader_payoff: A hurried invocation can matter as an act that assigns value and allegiance, not only as an inward wish.
findings.containment: This is exploratory: the focus verb may carry only its status-making sense while 17:11 diagnoses haste separately. No particular harmful power is named, and ordinary prayer is not equated with making a deity.

epistemic.reason: The exact calling, good-and-evil, haste, and focus coordinates are present, but the speech-act connection is an inference from a legacy_unbound trace and a qualified naming facet.

findings.title: No borrowed bearer
findings.claim: The pericope first warns against taking a wakil apart from God, then fastens each person's record to that person, calls the self sufficient for its account, and denies that one burden-bearer can carry another's load. Against the focus's blamed and forsaken result, the rival can be read as a failed substitute for personal accountability.
findings.mechanism: Entrusting in 17:2 meets the attached record and self-account in 17:13-14 and the non-transferable burden in 17:15; the focus's makhdulan and madhmuman return the result as lost support and blame. The sequence changes forsakenness from simply lacking a helper into the failure of a hoped-for liability-bearer.
findings.reader_payoff: Being left unsupported now includes having no one who can take over the personal account or carry the person's burden.
findings.containment: The focus does not explicitly say that the rival was chosen as a guarantor, and worship and liability transfer may be adjacent failures. The reading does not specify a judgment beyond what the supplied personal-account sequence supports.

epistemic.reason: The pericope supplies exact traces for entrusting, attachment, account, and non-transfer, but the failed-guarantor relation is explicitly an inference in a legacy_unbound HFT record.

findings.title: A counter-assigned outcome
findings.claim: The focus prohibits a human from assigning another deity, then marks the consequence with fa and blame. At 17:18, desire for the immediate is followed by a divine assignment of an adverse destination and the same blame state, so the focus can echo a counter-assignment directed back toward its maker.
findings.mechanism: The focus's jaʿala and madhmuman meet the repeated jaʿala and madhmuman in 17:18; the earlier desire and hastening specify the route into that outcome, while expulsion echoes the focus's loss of support. The repeated result changes a generic warning into a possible reply-pattern between human assignment and assigned consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's consequence recalls a concrete earlier outcome in the pericope instead of remaining a free-standing warning.
findings.containment: The repeated formula may link outcomes without strict measure-for-measure causality. The focus remains a prohibition with a consequence, not a claim that every act receives an identical repayment.

epistemic.reason: The repeated making and blame forms and the exact 17:18 trace are supplied; a retributive reversal is the HFT reader inference and remains qualified.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: birini veya şeyi belirli bir duruma getirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Var olan bir katılımcının durumunu, niteliğini veya konumunu değiştiren ettirici işlemi bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's human maker uses jaʿala to assign deity-status to a rival.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: At 17:18, the same making verb assigns an adverse destination to the person who desires the immediate.
branch_activations.activation: Human status-assignment meets divine outcome-assignment in the repeated verb, making the focus's consequence readable as a counter-assignment.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The maker of a rival may in turn be made into one who receives an adverse outcome.
branch_activations.boundary: The repeated verb does not by itself prove strict reciprocal causation.

findings.title: The rival as another horizon
findings.claim: The focus calls the rival akhar, another or later. In 17:18-21, the immediate and what comes after the first organize desire, striving, and relative degree; the rival can therefore function as an alternate ultimate horizon rather than only another being in a list.
findings.mechanism: The focus's core other-or-after-first branch stays on its adjective, while the later-horizon language in 17:18-19 and the degrees of 17:21 supply a distinct temporal trigger. Their contact lets another deity stand functionally for an alternative end that can organize desire and work.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning can reach the direction in which desire and effort are organized, not only the number of named divine objects.
findings.containment: The focus adjective is not translated as al-akhirah, and the rival is not identified with the afterlife. Ordinary otherness remains intact; the temporal-horizon reading is functional and exploratory.

epistemic.reason: The focus's other/later branch and exact desire, striving, and rank traces are supplied, but treating a deity as an ultimate horizon is an attributed functional inference.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The explicit later-horizon term in 17:19 is desired and pursued.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's otherness meets the pericope's desired later horizon without merging the two forms, turning the rival into a possible alternative end.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Another deity can function as an alternate horizon of desire and effort.
branch_activations.boundary: The adjective is not given the noun's afterlife sense; this is a functional contextual reading.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The deity warning can also concern what receives a person's final allegiance.
branch_activations.boundary: No claim is made that the focus literally names desire, striving, or the afterlife.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The rival can stand functionally across from the immediate horizon.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not itself name the immediate term, and the contrast remains contextual.

findings.title: Exclusive worship and requested aid
findings.claim: As an external overlay, 1:5 pairs worship and asking for aid directed to God alone. Against the focus's warning against another deity and its ending in forsakenness, this supplies a positive communal posture of exclusive worship and sought support.
findings.mechanism: The focus's ilah branch carries the worship relation and its makhdulan branch carries withdrawn support; the two declarations in 1:5 provide distinct triggers for both. This adds an affirmative first-person plural enactment to the pericope's warning without changing the focus's wording.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast becomes not only between one deity and another, but between divided allegiance and a shared practice of worship and seeking aid from one source.
findings.containment: This is limited to the supplied 1:5 surface as a specific overlay. It does not make the focus itself a prayer, import a whole-Fatiha theme, or equate worship with aid.

epistemic.reason: The exact external ayah surface and root occurrences are supplied and contact directly with focus branches; the communal counterpart is an ayah-specific inference, with no separate source-trust label in the packet.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus names God and another deity object within the worship relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The exact 1:5 surface says we worship You and we ask You for aid.
branch_activations.activation: The exclusive worship declaration meets the focus's rival deity object and makes divided versus directed worship newly visible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's prohibition can be read against a positive practice of worship directed to one source.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus itself remains a prohibition, not the first-person plural declaration.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's ilahan names the worshipped object.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The fronted You in 1:5 is the direct object of both worship and asking for aid.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's rival worship-object meets the external line's single addressee, making the object of allegiance explicit.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Another deity is contrasted with worship and aid directed to one addressee.
branch_activations.boundary: The object sense remains paired with its worship core; the focus does not itself state the 1:5 address.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kimseye yapılan yardımı ve verilen desteği keserek onu desteksiz bırakma.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's makhdulan names the person left without aid.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The distinct 1:5 declaration asks the single addressee for aid.
branch_activations.activation: Seeking aid from one source meets the focus's state of being left without aid, making forsakenness the inverse of the positive relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's abandonment becomes perceptible against a communal act of asking one source for help.
branch_activations.boundary: This adds no broader Fatiha theme and does not claim the two ayat describe the same speaker or event.
